proposal.explanation: The trace mismatches on o_data show unexpected zeroes during active valid/ready handshake cycles after reset deassertion. This points to conditions incorrectly gating data flow or output registers holding zero due to reset-sensitive qualifiers missing. The top candidates add !i_reset guards to readiness (o_ready), the r_valid set condition, and the o_valid generation path, directly aligning state transitions with the post-reset operational window. The r_valid condition (line 137) and o_ready assignment (line 160) are the most upstream handshake gates; qualifying them with !i_reset prevents premature or stalled valid assertions. The o_valid initial condition (line 133) and the r_valid else-if gate (line 140) are secondary but related. The rhs substitutions (w_data, i_data) address the symptom (zero payload) but not the root gating cause, so they rank lower.

proposal.explanation: The o_data output is stuck at 0 because multiple combinational and sequential assignments drive 0 instead of the correct data sources. The highest-priority fixes directly target the failing o_data assignments by substituting the appropriate data signals (w_data or i_data) for the hardcoded 0. The passthrough path and both output register configurations (NET_OUTPUT and REG_OUTPUT) each have sites where 0 is assigned to o_data. Structural coverage shows these are the exact failure targets. Lower-priority condition_gate patches adjust r_valid control logic but don't directly fix the data path driving o_data=0.

proposal.explanation: The failure shows o_data stuck at 0 while expected values appear at cycles 6-27. The root cause is that r_valid never gets set during reset release because the condition at line 135 requires (i_valid && o_ready) && (o_valid && !i_ready), but o_valid depends on r_valid creating a circular dependency. patch_30270cbdad9d fixes the clear path so r_valid can clear when i_ready asserts without requiring i_valid. The w_data substitutions (patches c9c4ad33c838, 14fa1671138d, e9c2e7485e9b, 97ba2adecc6f) ensure registered data reaches o_data instead of hard zeros. The r_valid set guards (patches da55a60398f6, 042f4158d3f0, 233b0c340b70) prevent spurious sets during reset or invalid input phases.

proposal.explanation: The simulation mismatches show o_data stuck at 0 when it should carry valid payload values (65, 253, 184, 143, 121). The highest-relevance candidates directly substitute the correct data signals (i_data or w_data/r_data) into the o_data combinational assignments where 0 is currently driven. patch_1f207853dea8 and patch_e9c2e7485e9b target the NET_OUTPUT combinational path; patch_97ba2adecc6f targets the REG_OUTPUT sequential path. The condition_gate candidates adjust r_valid control logic around reset and valid qualification, which may fix the valid/ready handshake that gates data flow, but they do not directly supply data to o_data and show lower structural coverage of the failure site.
